players.product: AI servers and high-end computers: scaleX640 single-cabinet 640-card supernode, scaleX40 cable-free box supernode and scaleX supercluster; HPC systems; ParaStor / FlashNexus storage; immersion and cold-plate liquid cooling

quarterly_data.quarter: Sugon results briefing Q&A: H1 2026 collective (09-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Chairman and general manager Li Jun and independent director Zheng Yongqin (H1 2026 collective results briefing): the National Supercomputing Internet Zhengzhou node went officially online in July; the company has set up a project operating company jointly with the government that provides technical support and operating services for the Zhengzhou core node, whose hundred-thousand-card cluster supports large-model training, scientific computing and AI inference at the same time and serves users through the National Supercomputing Internet. Operating income will ultimately depend on the contracts the company signs with customers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sugon results briefing Q&A: H1 2026 collective (09-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Independent director Zheng Yongqin (results briefing): subsidiary Sugon Shuchuang has ranked first by market share in China's compute-center infrastructure thermal-management equipment market for five consecutive years (company claim) and keeps a leading share in the domestic business of some leading internet companies; it continues to expand in overseas compute-center liquid cooling and, as of H1 2026, had taken on overseas liquid-cooling projects (by project location) of more than 600MW cumulatively. Li Jun: liquid cooling has become the inevitable choice for next-generation infrastructure as high-density AI compute expands, and converting existing air-cooled rooms and servers to liquid cooling is a rigid need for upgrading existing data centers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sugon results briefing Q&A: H1 2026 collective (09-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Commercialisation and business model (results briefing): independent director Zheng Yongqin said the supernode, high-speed network, high-end storage and high-performance computing platform products released since the start of 2026 have been commercially delivered one after another, though some may still take time to move from commercial delivery to large-scale industrialisation; CFO and board secretary Weng Qinan said FlashNexus 9000 and other high-end storage have been deployed. Weng: high-end computers and other compute equipment remain the core business and were the main driver of H1 growth; compute services (its platform links several compute centers and runs them on commission) are still a low share of revenue; compute demand is fairly strong and utilisation high, though future demand may be uncertain with AI development; the company is not engaged in large-scale capex expansion; line capacity matches the current order scale; contracts on hand will be delivered and recognised in H2 per contract schedules with no default risk, and agreed prepayments and milestone payments are used to improve operating cash flow.

quarterly_data.quarter: Sugon results briefing Q&A: H1 2026 collective (09-03-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Positioning (results briefing): Li Jun said the company is the chair unit of the National Supercomputing Internet (compute network) and builds and operates the national unified compute-scheduling platform, and has built a full 'chip - device - cloud - compute' chain; he and CFO Weng Qinan said it is one of the few vendors able to stably deliver ten-thousand-card and even hundred-thousand-card domestic clusters (company claim). Weng: designs for different chips need some customisation, but core components of its high-end computers are relatively general and do not hurt delivery efficiency. On Hygon Information Technology, Li Jun said the two keep long-standing industrial cooperation (Hygon focusing on chips, Sugon on compute-infrastructure deployment) and whether or not they restructure does not affect it.
